## Generating the Table: Parameters Are Embedded {.smaller}

Typical implementation — key parameters **hardcoded** directly in the script:

```{.r code-line-numbers="5,7,13,18"}
library(tidyverse)

# Safety population
adsl_safe <- adsl %>%
  filter(SAFFL == "Y")              # <- hardcoded

n_trt <- count(adsl_safe, TRTA)    # <- hardcoded

# Treatment-emergent AEs
adae_te <- adae %>%
  filter(
    USUBJID %in% adsl_safe$USUBJID,
    TRTEMFL == "Y"                  # <- hardcoded
  )

# Count by System Organ Class and Preferred Term
result <- adae_te %>%
  group_by(AESOC, AEDECOD, TRTA) %>%  # <- hardcoded
  summarise(n = n_distinct(USUBJID), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_trt, by = "TRTA") %>%
  mutate(
    pct  = round(n.x / n.y * 100, 1),
    cell = sprintf("%d (%.1f)", n.x, pct)
  )
```

> Every filter, variable name, and hierarchy is **buried in the code**.  
> Changing the population means hunting through the script.

## Separating Parameters from Code {.smaller}

Pull parameters into a **YAML metadata file** — the code becomes generic:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
**`analysis_config.yaml`**

```yaml
population:
  dataset:  ADSL
  variable: SAFFL
  value:    "Y"

events:
  dataset:  ADAE
  variable: TRTEMFL
  value:    "Y"

grouping:
  variable: TRTA

subject_id: USUBJID

hierarchy:
  - AESOC
  - AEDECOD
```
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
**R code — driven by metadata**

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(yaml)

cfg <- read_yaml("analysis_config.yaml")

# Population — from metadata
adsl_safe <- adsl %>%
  filter(.data[[cfg$population$variable]] ==
           cfg$population$value)
n_trt <- count(adsl_safe,
               .data[[cfg$grouping$variable]])

# Events — from metadata
adae_te <- adae %>%
  filter(
    USUBJID %in% adsl_safe$USUBJID,
    .data[[cfg$events$variable]] ==
      cfg$events$value
  )

# Hierarchy — from metadata
result <- adae_te %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(
    c(cfg$hierarchy, cfg$grouping$variable)
  ))) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n_distinct(.data[[cfg$subject_id]]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
:::
:::

## Metadata Quickly Grows {.smaller}

One AE table means **many** analyses. The YAML expands rapidly:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```yaml
reporting_event:
  id: "RE-AE-001"
  label: "AE Summary Table"

  analysis_sets:
    - id: AS001
      label: "Safety Analysis Set"
      condition:
        dataset:    ADSL
        variable:   SAFFL
        comparator: EQ
        value:      "Y"

  data_subsets:
    - id: DS001
      label: "Treatment-Emergent AEs"
      condition:
        variable: TRTEMFL
        value:    "Y"
    - id: DS002
      label: "Serious TEAEs"
      conditions:
        - {variable: TRTEMFL, value: "Y"}
        - {variable: AESER,   value: "Y"}
    - id: DS003
      label: "TEAEs leading to D/C"
      conditions:
        - {variable: TRTEMFL, value: "Y"}
        - {variable: AEACN,   value: "WITHDRAWN"}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```yaml
  groupings:
    - id: GF001
      groupingVariable: TRTA
      dataDriven: false
      groups:
        - {id: G1, label: "Treatment A"}
        - {id: G2, label: "Treatment B"}
        - {id: G3, label: "Total"}

  methods:
    - id: M001
      label: "n and percent"
      operations:
        - {id: OP1, label: "n",
           function: COUNT_DISTINCT}
        - {id: OP2, label: "%",
           function: PERCENT_BY_SUBSET}

  analyses:
    - {id: AN001, label: ">=1 TEAE",
       dataset:     ADAE,
       analysisSet: AS001,
       dataSubset:  DS001,
       grouping:    GF001,
       method:      M001}
    - {id: AN002, label: "Serious TEAE",
       dataset:     ADAE,
       analysisSet: AS001,
       dataSubset:  DS002,
       grouping:    GF001,
       method:      M001}
    # ... 30+ more analyses per table
    # ... 100s of tables per study
```


:::
:::
::: {.complexity-note}
Without a **schema**, this is unvalidated.  
Without a **standard**, every team invents their own format.
:::

# Analysis Results Standard {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## ARS v1.0: Background {.smaller}

**What it defines**

- A formal **metadata model** for every clinical analysis
- Connects ADaM datasets (inputs) to results (outputs)
- Covers concetps like populations, filters, groupings, methods, operations

**Why it matters**

- Unambiguous — no programmer interpretation required
- Reproducible — any compliant tool gives the same result
- Auditable — every result traces to a specification
- Automatable — machines can execute the metadata directly

**The ARS Stack**

<table class="ae-table" style="margin-top: 0.8em;">
<thead>
<tr>
  <th>Layer</th>
  <th>Purpose</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><strong>LinkML</strong></td>
  <td>The blueprint that defines and validates the ARS structure</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><strong>ARS (before execution)</strong></td>
  <td>A machine-readable analysis specification</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><strong>ARS (after execution)</strong></td>
  <td>The same specification, now enriched with results</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><strong>ARD</strong></td>
  <td>The analysis results represented as structured result records that can be extracted from the completed ARS</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Demystifying ARS, ARD, and LinkML {.smaller}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.5em; font-size: 1.1em;"}
**ARS = Recipe**  
The specification that describes *what* to analyze and *how* to compute it

**ARD = Cooked Meal**  
The actual results produced by executing the ARS specification

**LinkML = Recipe Template**  
The schema that defines the structure and rules for writing valid recipes
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 1.5em; font-size: 0.85em; background: #f5f5f5; padding: 1em; border-radius: 5px; border-left: 4px solid #2563eb;"}
**Key Insight:** ARS starts as a specification document. After execution, it can also contain the resulting ARD — the specification and its results travel together.
:::

## Worked Example: From Spec to Results {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**ARS Specification (Recipe)**

```yaml
analysis:
  id: AN001
  label: "Mean Age by Treatment"
  dataset: ADSL
  variable: AGE
  
analysisSet:
  condition: SAFFL == "Y"
  
grouping:
  variable: TRTA
  
method:
  operation: MEAN
```

<span style="color: #2563eb; font-weight: 600;">↓ Execute</span>
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**ARD (Cooked Meal)**

```yaml
results:
  - analysisId: AN001
    groupId: "Placebo"
    value: 42.3
    
  - analysisId: AN001
    groupId: "Treatment A"
    value: 43.1
    
  - analysisId: AN001
    groupId: "Treatment B"
    value: 41.8
```

<span style="color: #16a34a; font-weight: 600;">✓ Results</span>
:::
:::

::: {style="margin-top: 0.8em; font-size: 0.78em; color: #555;"}
**LinkML** ensures both the specification and results follow the same schema — any tool that understands ARS can read and execute this.
:::



## The ARS Model: Focus on some of the core classes for ARD generation {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'theme':'default', 'themeVariables': { 'fontSize':'9px', 'fontFamily':'arial'}}}%%
classDiagram
    direction TB

    class ReportingEvent {
        string id
        string label
    }
    class Analysis {
        string id
        string label
        string dataset
        string analysisVariable
    }
    class AnalysisSet {
        string id
        string label
        string condition
    }
    class DataSubset {
        string id
        string label
        string condition
    }
    class GroupingFactor {
        string id
        string groupingVariable
        boolean dataDriven
    }
    class AnalysisMethod {
        string id
        string label
    }
    class Operation {
        string id
        string label
        string resultPattern
    }

    ReportingEvent "1" --> "*" Analysis : contains
    Analysis "1" --> "1" AnalysisSet : analysisSet
    Analysis "1" --> "0..1" DataSubset : dataSubset
    Analysis "1" --> "1..*" GroupingFactor : orderedGroupings
    Analysis "1" --> "1" AnalysisMethod : method
    AnalysisMethod "1" --> "1..*" Operation : operations
```
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}
::: {style="font-size: 0.65em; line-height: 1.5;"}
`AnalysisSet` = **who** (population)

`DataSubset` = **which records** (event filter)

`GroupingFactor` = **how to split** (columns)

`Operation` = **what to compute**
:::
:::
:::
